title: Coverage Criteria and Order Values for PAP Therapy Equipment Device Classes
content:
# Coverage Criteria and Order Values — PAP Therapy Equipment

Each PAP Therapy Equipment device class has its own entry requirements and its own order values: the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, events per hour) on the qualifying sleep test at or above which the test alone qualifies the patient, a lower AHI that qualifies when documented symptoms or comorbidities are present, whether CPAP must first have been tried and proven ineffective, a left ventricular ejection fraction at or below which the class may not be furnished, whether the class delivers a backup respiratory rate, the highest pressure it delivers, whether any change of prescribed pressure needs a new written order, and how many calendar months a written order stays usable after its date to start therapy or a supply cycle.

## Entry requirements by class

| Device class | Diagnosis and test the class is furnished on |
|---|---|
| Travel CPAP System (E0601) | a valid written order for PAP therapy; self-pay only — a second or travel device is never billed to coverage |
| CPAP Fixed-Pressure System (E0601) | obstructive sleep apnea, on a facility or home sleep test, under the AHI values below |
| Auto-Adjusting CPAP System (E0601) | obstructive sleep apnea, on a facility or home sleep test, under the AHI values below |
| Bilevel PAP Spontaneous System (E0470) | obstructive sleep apnea, with CPAP tried and proven ineffective on a facility titration or home trial |
| Bilevel PAP Spontaneous-Timed System (E0471) | central or complex sleep apnea, or hypoventilation syndrome, on a facility polysomnogram |
| Adaptive Servo-Ventilation System (E0471) | central sleep apnea or Cheyne-Stokes respiration, on a facility polysomnogram, with a left ventricular ejection fraction above the class threshold |

## Values by class

| Device class | AHI alone (at or above) | AHI with symptoms or comorbidities (at or above) | Prior CPAP failure required | Ejection fraction threshold (percent) | Backup rate | Highest pressure (cmH2O) | New written order for any pressure change | Written order usable for (months) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Travel CPAP System (E0601) | 0 (no AHI rule) | 0 (no AHI rule) | no | 0 (no cardiac rule) | no | 20 | yes | 12 |
| CPAP Fixed-Pressure System (E0601) | 15 | 5 | no | 0 (no cardiac rule) | no | 20 | yes | 12 |
| Auto-Adjusting CPAP System (E0601) | 15 | 5 | no | 0 (no cardiac rule) | no | 20 | yes | 12 |
| Bilevel PAP Spontaneous System (E0470) | 15 | 5 | yes | 0 (no cardiac rule) | no | 25 | yes | 12 |
| Bilevel PAP Spontaneous-Timed System (E0471) | 15 | 5 | no | 0 (no cardiac rule) | yes | 30 | yes | 12 |
| Adaptive Servo-Ventilation System (E0471) | 15 | 5 | no | 45 | yes | 25 | yes | 12 |

A figure of 0 in an AHI or ejection fraction column means that no such rule applies to the class.

## Reading the values (hypothetical test results)

- A qualifying test with an AHI of 15.0 meets the 15 value of a CPAP class on its own; an AHI of 14.9 does not, but meets the 5 value when symptoms or comorbidities are documented.
- An AHI of 4.9 meets neither value of a CPAP class.
- For the Adaptive Servo-Ventilation System (E0471) the ejection fraction must be above 45 percent: 46 percent is above the threshold, 45 percent is at it and the class may not be furnished.
- A prescribed pressure of 28 cmH2O lies within the 30 cmH2O of the Bilevel PAP Spontaneous-Timed System (E0471) but beyond the 25 cmH2O of the Adaptive Servo-Ventilation System (E0471) and the 20 cmH2O of the CPAP classes.
